Q: Homebrew services. I can’t start the service and get "Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error" A:

To see the real errors, you need to run the service without Homebrew (executable brew)

I had a similar problem, but instead of MongoDB, I could not start Apache (HTTPd).

brew services start httpd

Output:

Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error
Try re-running the command as root for richer errors.
Error: Failure while executing; `/bin/launchctl bootstrap gui/501
/Users/john/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.httpd.plist` exited with
5.
FAIL: 1

Unfortunately Homebrew doesn't show the user what causes this error. At first, I tried to use the tips from the answers to this question, but neither reinstalling Apache nor unload -w/load -w helped. I also found nothing in the Homebrew logs. I decided to investigate Apache itself. To do this, I ran Apache without Homebrew:

/opt/homebrew/Cellar/httpd/2.4.51/bin/apachectl start

Output:

httpd: Syntax error on line 66 of /opt/homebrew/etc/httpd/httpd.conf: Cannot load /opt/homebrew/Cellar/php@5.6/5.6.40_3/lib/httpd/modules/libphp5.so into server: dlopen(/opt/homebrew/Cellar/php@5.6/5.6.40_3/lib/httpd/modules/libphp5.so, 0x000A): tried: '/opt/homebrew/Cellar/php@5.6/5.6.40_3/lib/httpd/modules/libphp5.so' (no such file), '/usr/local/lib/libphp5.so' (no such file), '/usr/lib/libphp5.so' (no such file)
FAIL: 1

Then it was finally clear what was the reason why the HTTPd service was not starting. It turned out that after the PHP upgrade, the PHP version had changed, and I forgot to write the new PHP version in the Apache configuration file.

I quickly fixed this and Apache started up.

Q: Is it normal that std::unorder_map has different bucket_counts? A:

Yes, this is normal. Try to implement a bucket-based map from scratch, and you will see that there is some degree of arbitrariness in the way the set of keys is broken into buckets. This classification is based on the value of the hash code obtained from every key. Every time you get a new key and its hash code, you have to decide if you have to create a new bucket or add this key to an existing bucket closest by the hash code value. Note that at the moment of this decision, you don't know the total number of key-value pairs in the map during its lifetime. These decisions is a matter of optimization, so you have a trade-off between the complexity of this calculation and the optimization of the set of buckets. There is always a trade-off between redundancy (and, hence, memory usage) and performance.
(Note that two extremes, either exactly 1 bucket or the number of buckets equal to the number of keys would defeat the purpose of the algorithm, leading to the time complexity of O(N), that is, always the worst-case scenario possible for the bucket system. The optimal decision will be somewhere in between.)

I am not sure if you put any difference in your sample compared to the sample on this page, but the number of buckets can be implementation-dependent. Note the word possible in possible output.

Q: React Codemirror import issue A:

So you are trying to import CodeMirror but the module does not have a default export, you can import it like this instead :

import * as CodeMirror from 'codemirror';

if you are using TypeScript add this line under compilerOptions in your tsconfig.json file :

allowSyntheticDefaultImports: true

Q: Convert file data to question marks in VS Code A:

As soon as you saved it in an encoding that didn't have your glyphs, the original data is gone. Your original characters are now literally question marks. You need to find a backup.
